name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.119.0 — The ```surfaces line grammar is parsed in exactly one place, `spec/scripts/lib/surfaces.js`, and `design-atlas.js` and `genesis-driver.js` both fold over it instead of carrying divergent copies; `genesis-driver.js` also drops its own synchronous stdout writer and fail-closed child runner for `lib/driver-io.js`, matching the review, build, and mocks drivers. Behavior is unchanged and both drivers shrink. 7.118.0 — Citation checker resolves prose-lookback citations instead of skipping them. A citation whose preceding words name no file ("authored against § Design Canon") is now checked against the citing file plus every file in spec/doctrine, derived from the directory so a new doctrine file joins with no edit. The resolution is deliberately weak: a heading matching nothing in that union stays SKIP and can never become a MISS, because ordinary English before a section mark cannot be told apart from a real file reference and a strong resolution there would turn correct doctrine red. Repo-wide coverage goes from CHECKED=88 SKIP=104 to CHECKED=158 SKIP=34, MISS still 0; the remainder are host-generated pipeline-rules sections the checker skips by design. 7.117.0 — Driver-stepped command files (build, review, run, mocks) stop restating what their drivers print at runtime — every envelope, exit, cap and remedy now arrives from the driver at the step where it is needed, once. Every command's Rules section is capped at 8 bullets and every shared-for section list is pinned exactly, so a section cannot join a command's read surface silently. The host pipeline-rules file is documented as path-scoped and arrives with the config Read, so no command re-reads it, and the genesis discovery brief is edited in place per answer and rendered in full only once, at discovery's end.
